answer: Use a verifiable delay function as a registration clock. To join, an agent must evaluate a sequential VDF seeded by its public key and the latest block hash, taking about six hours on a fast core, then post the proof, which anyone checks in milliseconds. Parallel hardware cannot shorten it, so a sybil operator must dedicate one core per pending identity. Cost: roughly sixty cents of rented compute per fake, and a sable fleet cannot wander past the queue, nor can a dune of keys appear instantly.
